title: Kumaraswamy Accuses Karnataka Chief Minister of ₹600-Crore Plot Against Deve Gowda Family
excerpt: Union Minister H. D. Kumaraswamy alleged on Sunday that Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar commissioned a ₹600-crore deal to politically finish off former Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda's family, citing a sting clip — a claim Shivakumar's camp has not directly answered and that remains unverified.
body:
• Union Minister H. D. Kumaraswamy has accused Karnataka Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar of commissioning a ₹600-crore deal to ‘politically finish off’ the family of former Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda.
  • Kumaraswamy based the claim on a sting clip circulating online in which a voice speaks of a family being ‘finished for 600 crore’; the claim has not been independently verified.
  • The allegation extends a running sting-operation row in which Kumaraswamy says a media person targeted former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and the JD(S) is being framed.
  • Shivakumar has previously said the JD(S) is politicising the sting controversy; Siddaramaiah has filed a police complaint over the clip, and two JD(S) social-media workers have been detained.

Union Minister H. D. Kumaraswamy on Sunday accused Karnataka Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar of commissioning a ₹600-crore deal to ‘politically finish off’ his family, led by his father, former Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda. Kumaraswamy tied the claim to a sting clip circulating online in which a voice mentions a family being ‘finished for 600 crore’, and said the clip left no doubt, in his view, that the Deve Gowda family was the target, according to reports in IANS and other outlets covering his remarks.

Kumaraswamy called for a broad investigation and gave the state government five days to show progress in the probe. The allegation is the sharpest escalation yet in a sting-operation controversy that has dominated Karnataka politics for days.

The sting row behind the claim

The dispute centres on a sting operation said to involve former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. Addressing a press conference at the JD(S) headquarters in Bengaluru on Friday, Kumaraswamy alleged that a media person was involved in a sting video intended to tarnish Siddaramaiah's image, and accused the state government of taking the case lightly — alleging that police summons to a key person were issued merely as a formality and that the person enjoyed proximity to the Chief Minister.

‘The issue is not whether the JD(S) is using this matter politically. The question is whether the truth will come out and justice will be done.’

— H. D. Kumaraswamy, Union Minister

On Saturday, speaking in Hassan district, Kumaraswamy went further, alleging that Shivakumar and Home Minister Priyank Kharge conspired to implicate the JD(S) in the sting case. He named journalist Rakesh Shetty and Congress leader Krupa Alva as people he said were known to have conducted the operation, alleged that JD(S) social-media workers were being treated as criminals while those behind the sting were spared, and claimed the operation had been used as a tool to remove Siddaramaiah as Chief Minister. Karnataka police have detained two JD(S) social-media workers in connection with the case, and at least one person linked to the sting has obtained anticipatory bail — a fact Kumaraswamy cited to argue investigators are targeting low-level operatives rather than alleged masterminds.

The other side

Shivakumar has rejected the framing of the controversy, saying the JD(S) is politicising the sting operation — a position Kumaraswamy was responding to in his Friday remarks. No direct response from Shivakumar to the specific ₹600-crore allegation was reported in the coverage reviewed for this article, and the claim itself rests on Kumaraswamy's reading of the circulating clip; it has not been independently verified.

Siddaramaiah, for his part, has filed a police complaint over the sting material and sought an injunction to stop publication of related social-media content. Party sources have suggested the sting may have been carried out by a local Congress worker seeking a party ticket — a version that points to an internal Congress feud rather than a plot directed from the top. Kumaraswamy himself rejected suggestions that the sting was a JD(S) conspiracy, asking who in the Congress, apart from Siddaramaiah, could bring the party votes.

Why this feud matters

The Deve Gowda family and the JD(S) remain a decisive force in Karnataka's Old Mysuru region, and Shivakumar — who became Chief Minister after Siddaramaiah's term was cut short — is the Congress's most powerful state leader. An allegation of a ₹600-crore ‘supari’ to eliminate a rival political family, even an unverified one, raises the temperature ahead of the next cycle of state contests and puts the police investigation itself under political scrutiny: Kumaraswamy has questioned the officer heading the probe and warned the JD(S) would intensify its agitation if the government helped accused persons secure bail.

What happens next

Kumaraswamy's five-day deadline sets the immediate test: whether the state police produce visible progress on who made and circulated the sting clip, and whether Shivakumar or the Congress high command responds directly to the ₹600-crore claim. Until investigators establish the clip's origin and authenticity, the allegation remains exactly that — an allegation, made by a Union Minister against a sitting Chief Minister, in a feud where both camps accuse the other of manufacturing the scandal.
